The road inside the tube is cold grey from outside, against Arcade's warm tunnel light. The exit is not over-exposed and the opening is darker than the tube (equal, not better). Stone bridges have a solid parapet instead of Arcade's balusters (equal, the parapet is worse). Pylon legs by day: sun side about 12 % brighter, shade side about 11 % darker than Arcade (model). result.verdict: Recommendation: do not put R4 into test build 2 as it stands. Two high-severity rendering bugs at night in the rain must be fixed first; everything else holds. R4 closes the gap the user saw. Rain and snow now fall in the air at every Effekte level, including the Steam Deck preset, and the package adds spray, the wet road with reflections, snow banks, the sun disc, an over-exposed tunnel exit, the police-light glow and a night law that lifts the limousine out of near-black. The gates pass (measured): F1–F7 fairness network-wide, Arcade golden 20 of 20 and 17 of 17 identical, 9 render-check files green with the same numbers as R4's own run, cold shader cache at N1 and N2 with 0 compiles during the drive (the base compiled 3 at N1), and run_tests with only two load-dependent tests failing that R4 did not touch. Bug B1: the rear-lamp reflections are horizontal quads, so wherever the road ahead climbs they float as a red column above distant cars, in my N2N picture and in R4's own clip at 6.2 s. Bug B2: on the wet road the low-beam patch is 1.77× as bright as in Arcade and the base, and lane markings there have less than half their contrast, because the mirrored sky is mixed into the albedo and then lit by the headlights. I tried a 16-line fix for B2 in a scratch copy and measured the cone at 54 (Arcade 61) with marking contrast 3.30 (Arcade 2.93). No R4 check catches either bug, and mutation testing showed the snow-bank mesh and the after-glow continuity are not guarded either. By day, in snow, at dusk and inside tunnels Modern is now equal to or clearly better than Arcade; at night in the rain it is better in the air but worse on the road. The paint is still open: the GT reads grey at night (already so in the base) and the limousine is too saturated at night and pale at dusk. Steam Deck behaviour is inferred only; all numbers come from llvmpipe.

result.verdict: I found no blocker in R5 (5558bdc). It stays inside its files except for one golden line, Arcade is bit-identical (20/20 and 17/17), and every bridge and tunnel of the network (122 + 28, dev stage included) builds headless. Each one has exactly the parts Arcade's events give it: pylons, beacons, cables, truss portals, bridge lamps, banks at both ends, niches and the end cap. Nothing R5 builds stands over a lane below 4.5 m, no cable is closer than 2.15 m to a lane, no portal hill sits in an approach sight corridor, and modern_sight/modern_path_check --full are green. The package render checks and the ZS1 guards (K1 0.000 %) pass. R5's delivered pictures are bit-identical to my renders of its head, so its picture evidence is genuine. By day Modern is clearly better than Arcade and than the base at tunnels and bridges: tube panels, walkways and niches; water with real banks instead of a lake to the horizon; thin cables instead of rods; truss girders with shadows. It is worse than Arcade in four places: tunnel portals at night (lit to the top by the low beam; at the Gotthard R5's frame and hill are even a little brighter than the base), the road inside the tube seen from outside, the tunnel exit without over-exposure, and the solid parapet on stone bridges. Only the night-portal problem has a part R5 can fix in its own file. The full test run had 3 timing failures (two real-time audio checks, attract idle); alone they failed on the base just as often, and the music check runs with Arcade graphics, so none of them comes from R5. The new tests caught 18 of 22 deliberately broken rules; three rules (bridge lamps, Arcade's 7 cables per side, the set_zone guard) are not protected at all, and night_albedo is caught only through a script error. Performance on the bridge stretch is the same as the base. One commit peak of 6.88 ms at the Gotthard (deck budget 3 ms) did not repeat in a second run (0.59 ms).
